entries.name: unbound-check-removed
entries.claim: The rule's unbound half is what refuses a declared permission nothing acknowledges: comparing the acknowledgement lookup against null instead of undefined makes the branch unreachable, and a permission declared on the composed application with no acknowledgement then compiles silently -- the exact vacuum R7 named.

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: a permission the composed application declares and nothing acknowledges refuses the release by name
kills.expected: a declared permission that nothing binds and nothing acknowledges must refuse compilation

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: removing the acknowledgement of a permission the package still declares refuses it by name
kills.expected: a declared permission whose acknowledgement was removed must be refused by name

entries.name: acknowledgement-entry-removed
entries.claim: Removing one acknowledgement entry for a permission the composed application still declares (party_create) refuses the unchanged composed application by that permission's name; the admission twin is the same test passing with production restored, which the runner measures before mutating.

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: the unchanged composed application builds, and the acknowledgement is exactly its declared census

entries.name: stale-entry-added
entries.claim: An acknowledgement entry naming a permission the composed application does not declare, on a resource it does declare, refuses the unchanged composed application as stale by that entry's name: the list cannot rot.

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: the unchanged composed application builds, and the acknowledgement is exactly its declared census

entries.name: stale-check-removed
entries.claim: The rule's stale half is what refuses an entry naming a permission the package no longer declares while its resource is still present: keying the presence check on the permission id (never an entity id) instead of the entry's resource makes the branch unreachable, and a stale entry then survives compilation.

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: an entry naming a permission the package no longer declares is stale while its resource is present
kills.expected: an acknowledgement naming a permission the package does not declare must be refused as stale

entries.name: governed-package-key-renamed
entries.claim: Governance is keyed by package id and the composed application's key is load-bearing: renaming it leaves the composed application ungoverned, so the release compiles with an unacknowledged permission and the census test finds no governed package -- the subject-absent vacuity vector, closed by the census test rather than by the rule.

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: the unchanged composed application builds, and the acknowledgement is exactly its declared census
kills.expected: the composed application package must be governed by the unbound-permission acknowledgement

kills.name: unbound-permission acknowledgement: a permission the composed application declares and nothing acknowledges refuses the release by name
kills.expected: a declared permission that nothing binds and nothing acknowledges must refuse compilation
